intro: Lahore's Badshahi Mosque, one of the great Mughal monuments. This is the opening of its Urdu Wikipedia article plus the first lines of the history section.

sentences.urdu: بادشاہی مسجد 1673 میں اورنگزیب عالمگیر نے لاہور میں بنوائی۔
sentences.english: Aurangzeb Alamgir had the Badshahi Mosque built in Lahore in 1673.

sentences.urdu: یہ عظیم الشان مسجد مغلوں کے دور کی ایک شاندار مثال ہے اور لاہور شہر کی شناخت بن چکی ہے۔
sentences.english: This magnificent mosque is a splendid example of the Mughal era and has become the symbol of the city of Lahore.

sentences.urdu: یہ فیصل مسجد اسلام آباد کے بعد پورے پاکستان کی دوسری بڑی مسجد ہے، جس میں بیک وقت 60 ہزار لوگ نماز ادا کرسکتے ہیں۔
sentences.english: After the Faisal Mosque in Islamabad, it is the second-largest mosque in all of Pakistan; 60,000 people can pray in it at the same time.

sentences.urdu: اس مسجد کا انداز تعمیر جامع مسجد دلی سے بہت ملتا جلتا ہے جو اورنگزیب کے والد شاہجہان نے 1648 میں تعمیر کروائی تھی۔
sentences.english: The mosque's architectural style closely resembles the Jama Masjid in Delhi, which Aurangzeb's father Shah Jahan had built in 1648.

sentences.urdu: ہندوستان کے چھٹے مغل بادشاہ اورنگزیب عالمگیر تمام مغلوں میں سے سب سے زیادہ مذہبی بادشاہ تھے۔
sentences.english: Aurangzeb Alamgir, the sixth Mughal emperor of India, was the most religious of all the Mughal emperors.

sentences.urdu: انھوں نے اس مسجد کو اپنے سوتیلے بھائی مظفر حسین، جن کو فدائی خاں کوکہ بھی کہا جاتا تھا، کی زیر نگرانی تعمیر کروایا۔
sentences.english: He had this mosque built under the supervision of his stepbrother Muzaffar Hussain, who was also known as Fidai Khan Koka.

چکی: already (f.; completed action) (“ban chuki hai” = has become)
اسلام: Islam (here part of “Islamabad”, written as two words)
بیک: at one (“bayak waqt” = at the same time)
ادا: performed (“namaaz ada karna” = to offer prayers)
کرسکتے: can do (pl.; written as one word) (“kar sakte hain” = can)
کروائی: had (it) made (f.) (“taameer karwaai thi” = had had built)
کوکہ: Koka (Mughal title for a foster brother)
کہا: said; called (“kaha jaata tha” = was called)
جاتا: (passive helper, m.) (“kaha jaata tha” = was called)
زیر: under (“ki zer-e-nigraani” = under the supervision of)

questions.english: Who had the Badshahi Mosque built?

questions.urdu: بادشاہی مسجد میں ایک ساتھ کتنے لوگ نماز پڑھ سکتے ہیں؟
questions.english: How many people can pray in the Badshahi Mosque at once?

questions.urdu: اس مسجد کا انداز تعمیر کس مسجد سے ملتا جلتا ہے؟
questions.english: Which mosque does its architectural style resemble?

questions.urdu: مسجد کی تعمیر کی نگرانی کس نے کی؟
questions.english: Who supervised the building of the mosque?
